description.text: Faustina minore was betrothed to her cousin, the future emperor Marco Aurelio, in 139 and married him in 145.  In 147 she was elevated to the rank of Augusta, a title that reflected her prominence within the imperial family.

She accompanied Marco Aurelio on his northern campaigns (170‑174) and on the eastern expedition that followed the usurpation of Avidio Cassio.  Faustina died during a stop at Halala in southern Cappadocia in the summer of 175, after which her husband deified her, built a temple in Rome in her honor, and founded a charitable fund for girls called the second Puellae Faustinae.

curiosities.text: Faustina’s portraits and coins depict her with a simple hairstyle divided into two soft bands tied in a low knot, though some versions show a more elaborate braid reminiscent of her mother, Faustina maior.

The Historia Augusta records that Faustina entertained sailors and gladiators at her luxurious villa in Gaeta, and that she allegedly had a relationship with a gladiator who may have fathered her son Commodo.
After her death, the emperor founded the colony of Faustinopolis at the site of her passing, and the Baths of Faustina in Miletus were dedicated to her memory.
Faustina and Marco Aurelio had at least fourteen children, including two sets of twins, but only six survived to adulthood.
